"Decide what the git repo contains: (a) raw bundle JSON snapshot (current export format), (b) per-row files organized by relation (more diff-friendly), or (c) hybrid. "Codex review of the companion plan feature.

What works: the persisted plan data is coherent. At review time there were two active plans, eleven pending steps, contiguous step positions starting at 1, no claimed/running steps missing agents, and no staged/offstage drift in io.bundle.aquameta.plan.

Changes requested before this becomes a dependable cross-agent coordination primitive:
1. Add DB-level checks for plan_step.position > 0 and nonblank companion.plan.title / companion.plan_step.title. The current NOT NULL checks still allow empty titles and negative positions.
2. Add DB-level checks that claimed/running steps have agent_id and claimed_at. The documented compare-and-swap claim convention works for cooperative SQL agents, but PGFS/REST/SQL all write the same rows, so invalid states should be rejected at the table boundary.
3. Decide whether updated_at should use now(), statement_timestamp(), or clock_timestamp(). now() is acceptable for transaction-level freshness, but it does not distinguish multiple updates inside one transaction.
4. For the new review feature, consider enforcing nonblank review_text and enforcing that a non-null plan_step_id belongs to the same plan_id. The current comment says this is by convention; a composite FK or trigger would make the row invariant match the model.

Overall: the feature is simple and usable, and the session_brief/claimable_step surfaces are the right direction. The remaining work is mostly tightening row invariants so all Aquameta interfaces preserve the same coordination semantics."

"ALTER TABLE bundle.repository ADD COLUMN git_url text. Nullable — bundles without a remote are fine. Update the bundle extension SQL file (extensions/bundle/) to match. No behavior change yet; this is schema only.\nDone when: column exists, extension SQL updated, bundle.commit() on io.bundle.core.repository reflects the change."
